title: Wah, Kya Jodi Hai! The Fresh Bollywood Pairings That Will Define the Rest of 2026.
excerpt: From a goddess and a superstar to Bollywood's first big same-sex flirtation, the second half of the year is built on couples we've never seen together. New chemistry is the new spectacle.
body:
There's a particular electricity to a first time. Established jodis arrive pre-loaded with expectation — we know how **Ranveer** and **Deepika** spark, how **Ranbir** and **Alia** settle into each other. But a new pairing? That's a gamble nobody has placed yet, and the second half of 2026 is stacked with them. Indian cinema has quietly decided that fresh chemistry is the most bankable spectacle of all — more than a ₹250-crore set piece, more than a returning superstar. Here are the new combinations worth clearing your calendar for.

**Ranbir Kapoor & Sai Pallavi — Ramayana**

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=ojzJZPZHwyE</youtube>


The big one. The pairing everyone has been circling since the first frame leaked. In Nitesh Tiwari's two-part mythological epic, **Ranbir Kapoor** plays Lord Ram opposite **Sai Pallavi's** Sita — and on paper it's almost too right. Ranbir brings a restrained, interior intensity; Sai Pallavi has the most expressive, lived-in face in Indian cinema, the kind that can make devotion look like a physical act. This isn't a romance built on heat. It's built on dignity, and that's a far harder thing to cast. Part 1 lands Diwali 2026, and if the chemistry holds, it could become the emotional anchor of a franchise designed to run for years.

**Alia Bhatt & Sharvari — Alpha**

Yash Raj Films just did something it has never done in its spy universe: handed the keys to two women. **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari** headline *Alpha*, and the trailer makes the dynamic clear — this isn't a heroine-and-her-friend setup, it's two leads with their own gravity. The trolls were predictably terrified, which is exactly how you know YRF made the right bet. Their photoshoots together have already set the internet gushing about the chemistry; the film arrives July 3, and it may be the most consequential casting decision the studio makes this decade.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZrMgo5k_LM/


**Kriti Sanon & Rashmika Mandanna — Cocktail 2**

Here's the one with a current running under it. *Cocktail 2* (out June 19) pairs **Shahid Kapoor** with both **Kriti Sanon** and **Rashmika Mandanna** — Shahid and Rashmika together for the very first time, their dynamic carrying a raw, unspoken tension. But the pairing everyone is actually whispering about is Kriti and Rashmika. Reports ahead of the trailer launch speculated about a same-sex romantic thread between the two women — and when asked directly, Kriti neither confirmed it nor waved it away.

> "Ally is unhinged and beautifully chaotic." — Kriti Sanon, on her Cocktail 2 character

That coyness is its own kind of statement. If the film leans in, it would be a genuinely bold step for mainstream Bollywood — and a far cry from the franchise's 2012 origins.

**Ram Charan & Janhvi Kapoor — Peddi**

A cross-industry collision. **Ram Charan** brings pan-India, larger-than-life scale; **Janhvi Kapoor** brings a softer, evolving versatility. Against the rooted, sports-drama backdrop of *Peddi* — already the year's biggest South Indian release, past ₹200 crore — their contrast is the whole appeal. He's the storm; she's the stillness it moves around.

**The newcomers worth knowing**

The most intriguing jodis are the ones with no baggage at all. **Rasha Thadani & Abhay Verma** in *Layka Layki* have that raw first-film energy — Abhay broke out in *Munjya*, Rasha is one of the most-watched newcomers in the business, and neither carries a fixed image yet. **Saiee Manjrekar & Raghav Juyal** in *Ikaai* are the deliberate mismatch — her emotional precision against his post-*Kill* intensity. And **Lakshya & Ananya Panday**, fresh off *Chand Mera Dil*, have already proven a breezy, youthful spark that suggests the rom-com isn't dead, just waiting for the right faces.

**Why the diaspora should care**

For NRI audiences, fresh pairings are more than gossip — they're a preview of which films will actually travel. The jodis that pop on screen are the ones that fill diaspora multiplexes in Edison, Southall and Brampton, the ones that become the family-outing event of a long weekend. Most of these films — *Cocktail 2*, *Alpha*, *Peddi*, and eventually *Ramayana* — are slated for wide international theatrical releases across the US, UK and Canada, with OTT and dubbed-language windows to follow on the major Indian streamers.

The old formula said you cast a proven couple and let nostalgia do the selling. 2026 is betting the opposite — that audiences are hungrier for the thrill of not knowing. Wah, kya jodi hai, indeed. We just don't know which ones yet.
